ov: A large, fish-eating bird of prey, brown above and white below, found near water on every continent except Antarctica. It hovers, then plunges feet first, often going completely under the water. It is the only living species in its family.
rg: Every continent except Antarctica. European birds winter in Africa and North American birds in South America; Australian birds stay put.
df: Fish, which make up 99% of its diet, usually 25–35 cm long; rarely small mammals, snakes or birds.
fx: It can close its nostrils to keep water out during a dive.
Its nests can be 2 m wide and weigh about 135 kg, and some sites have been used for 70 years.
